embedding_queries.text: A polynomial of the form z plus higher-order terms, with nonzero top coefficient, takes some point of every centered disk to a value of larger modulus than the radius.

Assume some closed disk of radius r is mapped into itself, rescale the polynomial by q(w)=p(rw)/r to get a holomorphic self-map of the unit disk fixing the origin with derivative one, and apply the equality case of Schwarz's lemma to get a rotation.

A holomorphic function from the unit disk to itself that fixes zero and has derivative of modulus one at zero is a rotation, so a polynomial with a nonzero higher-order coefficient cannot be such a map.
If two polynomials agree on infinitely many points they are equal, so comparing the top coefficient gives a contradiction.
The conclusion looks geometric, so one is tempted to estimate coefficients, but the working approach is to normalize to the unit disk and use Schwarz rigidity rather than inequalities.
